summary: Deer Lodge County, MT wooden L-4 lookout; built 1930s or 1940 (sources disagree), emergency use to 1970, cab collapsed before 2009, now ruins.

facts.status_note: Cab collapsed before 2009 per firelookout.com; a memoir describes it collapsing with pieces scattered; FFLA index lists Tower Standing (Ruins)

visit.trail_note: A road guide describes an unpaved summit road from Dry Creek Road that needs a 4x4 and is not plowed in winter. No source read says whether the site is open to visitors.

events.note: Blog memoir says the tower was constructed in 1940. Firelookout.com says only built in the 1930s (see corrections).
Guards stationed in a tent camp while the station ran as an emergency lookout (newspaper, Sept 1940, as quoted).
Sanders County Independent-Ledger, July 24, 1940: new tent lookout announced, to be erected soon after July 1 (as quoted).
Family of three from Anaconda to take over the post (Billings Gazette, July 1947, as quoted).
Last used for emergencies, per firelookout.com.

corrections.proposed: built in the 1930s per firelookout.com; 1940 per a memoir; sources disagree
corrections.why: Firelookout.com gives only the decade (built in the 1930's). The memoir says constructed in 1940, and a 1940 newspaper describes a new tent lookout being set up that summer. No source read gives 1930.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The brief's conflict lists firelookout.com as showing standing. The firelookout.com page itself says the cab collapsed before 2009, and the FFLA index says Tower Standing (Ruins). Kept ruins.
Firelookout.com says 1930s, the memoir says 1940, and a 1940 newspaper describes a tent lookout being set up. Recorded as disputed; the story says the sources disagree.
Firelookout.com names the Anaconda Fire Protective Association. Rex's page places the site in the Deer Lodge National Forest. Kept the firelookout.com name in facts.agency.
Firelookout.com gives 10' wooden L-4 with no explanation of what 10 feet measures. The 1956 survey says about 25 feet, which is the basis for 7.6 m.
Firelookout.com says 8 miles SSW of Anaconda; the 1956 survey says about 7 miles SSE. The story says the sources differ on direction.

notes_for_editor: Build date is disputed: 1930s (firelookout.com) against 1940 (memoir and 1940 tent-lookout reports); the story says so and the brief's 1930 is proposed for correction. Agency is disputed (AFPA vs Deer Lodge NF). Ruins status is confirmed by three sources. No source read describes the remains in detail or says whether the site is open to the public. Road guide starts at Dry Creek Road while the memoir names Mill Creek Road. The NGS name is Grassy Hill Lookout Tower. Two WebSearch calls were used.
